sanskrit: tīrthayātrā tathaivātra pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām jaṭāsurasya tatraiva vadhaḥ samupavarṇyate
english: The pilgrimage of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas is likewise described here, and the slaying of Jaṭāsura is narrated in that same context.

sanskrit: niyukto bhīmasenaś ca draupadyā gandhamādane yatra mandārapuṣpārthaṃ nalinīṃ tām adharṣayat
english: Bhīmasena, commissioned by Draupadī on the Gandhamādana mountain to fetch mandāra flowers, there assaulted that lotus lake.

sanskrit: yatrāsya sumahad yuddham abhavat saha rākṣasaiḥ yakṣaiś cāpi mahāvīryair maṇimatpramukhais tathā
english: There his great battle took place with the rākṣasas and also with the mighty yakṣas headed by Maṇimat.

sanskrit: āgastyam api cākhyānaṃ yatra vātāpibhakṣaṇam lopāmudrābhigamanam apatyārtham ṛṣer api
english: The tale of Agastya is also there — the devouring of Vātāpi, and the sage's approach to Lopāmudrā for the sake of offspring.

sanskrit: tataḥ śyenakapotīyam upākhyānam anantaram indro 'gnir yatra dharmaś ca ajijñāsañ śibiṃ nṛpam
english: Next in succession comes the tale of the hawk and the pigeon, where Indra, Agni, and Dharma tested King Śibi.

sanskrit: ṛśyaśṛṅgasya caritaṃ kaumārabrahmacāriṇaḥ jāmadagnyasya rāmasya caritaṃ bhūritejasaḥ
english: The story of Ṛśyaśṛṅga, a celibate from boyhood, and the deeds of Rāma Jāmadagnya of great splendour.

sanskrit: kārtavīryavadho yatra haihayānāṃ ca varṇyate saukanyam api cākhyānaṃ cyavano yatra bhārgavaḥ
english: The slaying of Kārtavīrya and the destruction of the Haihayas are described there, and likewise the tale of Sukanyā, where the sage Cyavana of the Bhārgava line appears.

sanskrit: śaryātiyajñe nāsatyau kṛtavān somapīthinau tābhyāṃ ca yatra sa munir yauvanaṃ pratipāditaḥ
english: At Śaryāti's sacrifice the Nāsatya twins made him a drinker of soma, and there that sage was restored to youth by them.

sanskrit: jantūpākhyānam atraiva yatra putreṇa somakaḥ putrārtham ayajad rājā lebhe putraśataṃ ca saḥ
english: Here too is the tale of Jantu, where King Somaka sacrificed his son to gain offspring and thereby obtained a hundred sons.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakrīyam atraiva vivāde yatra bandinam vijitya sāgaraṃ prāptaṃ pitaraṃ labdhavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Here too is the story of Aṣṭāvakra, where the sage, having defeated Bandin in debate and recovered him from the ocean, regained his father.

sanskrit: avāpya divyāny astrāṇi gurvarthe savyasācinā nivātakavacair yuddhaṃ hiraṇyapuravāsibhiḥ
english: Having obtained divine weapons for the sake of his teacher, the left-handed archer fought the Nivātakavacas, the dwellers of the golden city.

sanskrit: samāgamaś ca pārthasya bhrātṛbhir gandhamādane ghoṣayātrā ca gandharvair yatra yuddhaṃ kirīṭinaḥ
english: Pārtha's reunion with his brothers on the Gandhamādana mountain, and the Ghoṣayātrā, where Kirīṭin fought with the gandharvas.

sanskrit: punarāgamanaṃ caiva teṣāṃ dvaitavanaṃ saraḥ jayadrathenāpahāro draupadyāś cāśramāntarāt
english: Their return again to the Dvaitavana lake, and the abduction of Draupadī from her hermitage by Jayadratha.

sanskrit: yatrainam anvayād bhīmo vāyuvegasamo jave mārkaṇḍeyasamasyāyām upākhyānāni bhāgaśaḥ
english: Where Bhīma, swift as the wind, pursued him; and the tales told in portions within the Mārkaṇḍeya conversations.

sanskrit: saṃdarśanaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya saṃvādaś caiva satyayā vrīhidrauṇikam ākhyānam aindradyumnaṃ tathaiva ca
english: The vision of Kṛṣṇa and his dialogue with Satyā, the tale of the grain and the heron, and likewise the story of Indradyumna.

sanskrit: sāvitryauddālakīyaṃ ca vainyopākhyānam eva ca rāmāyaṇam upākhyānam atraiva bahuvistaram
english: The story of Sāvitrī and of Uddālaka's line, and the tale of the son of Vena, and here too the Rāmāyaṇa episode narrated at great length.

sanskrit: karṇasya parimoṣo 'tra kuṇḍalābhyāṃ puraṃdarāt āraṇeyam upākhyānaṃ yatra dharmo 'nvaśāt sutam jagmur labdhavarā yatra pāṇḍavāḥ paścimāṃ diśam
english: Here the theft of Karṇa's earrings by Purandara; and the tale of the forest-dweller, where Dharma instructed his son; where the Pāṇḍavas, having obtained their boons, went westward.

sanskrit: etad āraṇyakaṃ parva tṛtīyaṃ parikīrtitam atrādhyāyaśate dve tu saṃkhyāte paramarṣiṇā ekonasaptatiś caiva tathādhyāyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
english: This third parvan is celebrated as the Āraṇyaka; the great sage has enumerated in it two hundred chapters plus sixty-nine chapters further declared.

sanskrit: ekādaśa sahasrāṇi ślokānāṃ ṣaṭśatāni ca catuḥṣaṣṭis tathā ślokāḥ parvaitat parikīrtitam
english: Eleven thousand verses, six hundred more, and sixty-four additional verses — such is this parvan as enumerated.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ nibodhedaṃ vairāṭaṃ parvavistaram virāṭanagaraṃ gatvā śmaśāne vipulāṃ śamīm dṛṣṭvā saṃnidadhus tatra pāṇḍavā āyudhāny uta
english: Now understand in detail this expansive Virāṭa parvan: going to Virāṭa's city and seeing the great śamī tree in the cremation ground, the Pāṇḍavas deposited their weapons there.

sanskrit: yatra praviśya nagaraṃ chadmabhir nyavasanta te durātmano vadho yatra kīcakasya vṛkodarāt
english: Where, having entered the city, they lived in disguise; and where the wicked Kīcaka was slain by Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: gograhe yatra pārthena nirjitāḥ kuravo yudhi godhanaṃ ca virāṭasya mokṣitaṃ yatra pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Where the Kurus were defeated in battle by Pārtha at the cattle raid, and where the cattle wealth of Virāṭa was rescued by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: virāṭenottarā dattā snuṣā yatra kirīṭinaḥ abhimanyuṃ samuddiśya saubhadram arighātinam
english: Where Uttarā was given by Virāṭa as a daughter-in-law to Kirīṭin, pledged to Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadrā, the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: caturtham etad vipulaṃ vairāṭaṃ parva varṇitam atrāpi parisaṃkhyātam adhyāyānāṃ mahātmanā
english: This extensive fourth parvan, the Virāṭa, has been described; here too the great soul has counted up the chapters.

sanskrit: saptaṣaṣṭir atho pūrṇā ślokāgram api me śṛṇu ślokānāṃ dve sahasre tu ślokāḥ pañcāśad eva tu parvaṇy asmin samākhyātāḥ saṃkhyayā paramarṣiṇā
english: Sixty-seven chapters complete — now hear from me the count of verses too: two thousand verses and fifty more are declared in this parvan by the reckoning of the supreme sage.

sanskrit: udyogaparva vijñeyaṃ pañcamaṃ śṛṇv ataḥ param upaplavye niviṣṭeṣu pāṇḍaveṣu jigīṣayā duryodhano 'rjunaś caiva vāsudevam upasthitau
english: The Udyoga parvan is to be known as the fifth; hear what follows: when the Pāṇḍavas were encamped at Upaplavya intent on victory, both Duryodhana and Arjuna came before Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: sāhāyyam asmin samare bhavān nau kartum arhati ity ukte vacane kṛṣṇo yatrovāca mahāmatiḥ
english: Having said, 'You should render us assistance in this war,' the great-minded Kṛṣṇa then spoke thus.

sanskrit: ayudhyamānam ātmānaṃ mantriṇaṃ puruṣarṣabhau akṣauhiṇīṃ vā sainyasya kasya vā kiṃ dadāmy aham
english: 'Shall I give to which of you my own self who will not fight but will serve as counsellor, O best of men, or an entire akṣauhiṇī of troops?'

sanskrit: vavre duryodhanaḥ sainyaṃ mandātmā yatra durmatiḥ ayudhyamānaṃ sacivaṃ vavre kṛṣṇaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The dull-witted Duryodhana of wicked mind chose the army, while Dhanaṃjaya chose Kṛṣṇa, who would not fight, as his counsellor.

sanskrit: saṃjayaṃ preṣayām āsa śamārthaṃ pāṇḍavān prati yatra dūtaṃ mahārājo dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pratāpavān
english: Where the mighty Mahārāja Dhṛtarāṣṭra dispatched Saṃjaya as an emissary to the Pāṇḍavas for the sake of peace.

sanskrit: śrutvā ca pāṇḍavān yatra vāsudevapurogamān prajāgaraḥ saṃprajajñe dhṛtarāṣṭrasya cintayā
english: And where, upon hearing of the Pāṇḍavas with Vāsudeva at their head, sleeplessness overtook Dhṛtarāṣṭra from his anxious brooding.

sanskrit: viduro yatra vākyāni vicitrāṇi hitāni ca śrāvayām āsa rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇam
english: Where Vidura caused King Dhṛtarāṣṭra the wise to hear words of varied import and wholesome counsel.

sanskrit: tathā sanatsujātena yatrādhyātmam anuttamam manastāpānvito rājā śrāvitaḥ śokalālasaḥ
english: Likewise where the king, afflicted with mental anguish and consumed by grief, was made to hear the supreme teaching on the Self from Sanatsujāta.

sanskrit: prabhāte rājasamitau saṃjayo yatra cābhibhoḥ aikātmyaṃ vāsudevasya proktavān arjunasya ca
english: Where, at the royal assembly at daybreak, Saṃjaya proclaimed before the king the unity of Vāsudeva and Arjuna.

sanskrit: yatra kṛṣṇo dayāpannaḥ saṃdhim icchan mahāyaśāḥ svayam āgāc chamaṃ kartuṃ nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Where Kṛṣṇa of great glory, moved by compassion and desiring peace, himself came to the city of Nāgasāhvaya to make reconciliation.

sanskrit: pratyākhyānaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya rājñā duryodhanena vai śamārthaṃ yācamānasya pakṣayor ubhayor hitam
english: And the rejection of Kṛṣṇa, who was beseeching on behalf of the good of both sides, by King Duryodhana.

sanskrit: karṇaduryodhanādīnāṃ duṣṭaṃ vijñāya mantritam yogeśvaratvaṃ kṛṣṇena yatra rājasu darśitam
english: Having perceived the wicked plotting of Karṇa, Duryodhana, and their allies, Kṛṣṇa there displayed his sovereignty as lord of yoga before the kings.

sanskrit: ratham āropya kṛṣṇena yatra karṇo 'numantritaḥ upāyapūrvaṃ śauṇḍīryāt pratyākhyātaś ca tena saḥ
english: Where Karṇa, mounted on the chariot, was persuaded by Kṛṣṇa through counsel; yet from his own valour and pride, he refused.

sanskrit: tataś cāpy abhiniryātrā rathāśvanaradantinām nagarād dhāstinapurād balasaṃkhyānam eva ca
english: Then also the march forth of chariots, horses, men, and elephants from the city of Hāstinapura, and the enumeration of the forces.

sanskrit: yatra rājñā ulūkasya preṣaṇaṃ pāṇḍavān prati śvobhāvini mahāyuddhe dūtyena krūravādinā rathātirathasaṃkhyānam ambopākhyānam eva ca
english: Where the king sent Ulūka as a harsh-spoken emissary to the Pāṇḍavas on the eve of the great battle; the enumeration of maharathas and rathas; and likewise the tale of Ambā.

sanskrit: etat subahuvṛttāntaṃ pañcamaṃ parva bhārate udyogaparva nirdiṣṭaṃ saṃdhivigrahasaṃśritam
english: This fifth parvan of the Bhārata, the Udyoga parvan, is designated as containing very many accounts and pertaining to peace and war.

sanskrit: adhyāyāḥ saṃkhyayā tv atra ṣaḍaśītiśataṃ smṛtam ślokānāṃ ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi tāvanty eva śatāni ca
english: In terms of count, one hundred and eighty-six chapters are noted here, and six thousand verses, and likewise that many hundreds.

sanskrit: ślokāś ca navatiḥ proktās tathaivāṣṭau mahātmanā vyāsenodāramatinā parvaṇy asmiṃs tapodhanāḥ
english: And ninety verses are declared, and likewise eight more, by the great-souled Vyāsa of noble mind in this parvan, O sages rich in austerity.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ vicitrārthaṃ bhīṣmaparva pracakṣate jambūkhaṇḍavinirmāṇaṃ yatroktaṃ saṃjayena ha
english: From this point on the Bhīṣma parvan of manifold import is told; the formation of the Jambū continent is described there by Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: yatra yuddham abhūd ghoraṃ daśāhāny atidāruṇam yatra yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ sainyaṃ viṣādam agamat param
english: Where a terrible, exceedingly dreadful battle raged for ten days; where the army of Yudhiṣṭhira fell into the deepest despondency.

sanskrit: kaśmalaṃ yatra pārthasya vāsudevo mahāmatiḥ mohajaṃ nāśayām āsa hetubhir mokṣadarśanaiḥ
english: Where the great-minded Vāsudeva destroyed Pārtha's faintness born of delusion through the reasoned arguments of the teaching of liberation.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya yatra pārtho mahādhanuḥ vinighnan niśitair bāṇai rathād bhīṣmam apātayat
english: Where Pārtha the great archer, placing Śikhaṇḍin in the van, struck Bhīṣma down from his chariot with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭham etan mahāparva bhārate parikīrtitam adhyāyānāṃ śataṃ proktaṃ saptadaśa tathāpare
english: This great sixth parvan of the Bhārata is celebrated; one hundred chapters are declared, and seventeen further.

sanskrit: pañca ślokasahasrāṇi saṃkhyayāṣṭau śatāni ca ślokāś ca caturāśītiḥ parvaṇy asmin prakīrtitāḥ vyāsena vedaviduṣā saṃkhyātā bhīṣmaparvaṇi
english: Five thousand verses, eight hundred more, and eighty-four verses are proclaimed in this parvan — so counted by the Veda-learned Vyāsa in the Bhīṣma parvan.

sanskrit: droṇaparva tataś citraṃ bahuvṛttāntam ucyate yatra saṃśaptakāḥ pārtham apaninyū raṇājirāt
english: Then is told the Droṇa parvan, varied and full of many accounts, where the Saṃśaptakas lured Pārtha away from the battlefield.

sanskrit: bhagadatto mahārājo yatra śakrasamo yudhi supratīkena nāgena saha śastaḥ kirīṭinā
english: Where Mahārāja Bhagadatta, equal to Śakra in battle, was slain by Kirīṭin together with his elephant Supratīka.

sanskrit: yatrābhimanyuṃ bahavo jaghnur lokamahārathāḥ jayadrathamukhā bālaṃ śūram aprāptayauvanam
english: Where many great warriors of the world, led by Jayadratha, slew Abhimanyu, the young hero who had not yet reached full youth.

sanskrit: hate 'bhimanyau kruddhena yatra pārthena saṃyuge akṣauhiṇīḥ sapta hatvā hato rājā jayadrathaḥ saṃśaptakāvaśeṣaṃ ca kṛtaṃ niḥśeṣam āhave
english: Abhimanyu being slain, where the enraged Pārtha in battle, having killed seven akṣauhiṇīs, slew King Jayadratha; and the destruction of the remaining Saṃśaptakas in the combat was accomplished fully.

sanskrit: alambusaḥ śrutāyuś ca jalasaṃdhaś ca vīryavān saumadattir virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ ghaṭotkacādayaś cānye nihatā droṇaparvaṇi
english: Alambusa, Śrutāyu, the valiant Jalasandha, Saumadatti, Virāṭa, the great warrior Drupada, Ghaṭotkaca and others were slain in the Droṇa parvan.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmāpi cātraiva droṇe yudhi nipātite astraṃ prāduścakārograṃ nārāyaṇam amarṣitaḥ
english: And here too Aśvatthāman, when Droṇa had fallen in battle, in his fury released the terrible Nārāyaṇa weapon.

sanskrit: saptamaṃ bhārate parva mahad etad udāhṛtam atra te pṛthivīpālāḥ prāyaśo nidhanaṃ gatāḥ droṇaparvaṇi ye śūrā nirdiṣṭāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: This great seventh parvan of the Bhārata is declared; it is here that those protectors of the earth, those heroic bulls among men designated in the Droṇa parvan, met their end for the most part.

sanskrit: adhyāyānāṃ śataṃ proktam adhyāyāḥ saptatis tathā aṣṭau ślokasahasrāṇi tathā nava śatāni ca
english: One hundred and seventy chapters are declared, and eight thousand verses and nine hundred more.

sanskrit: ślokā nava tathaivātra saṃkhyātās tattvadarśinā pārāśaryeṇa muninā saṃcintya droṇaparvaṇi
english: And nine verses likewise are here counted by the sage Pārāśarya, the seer of truth, having pondered the Droṇa parvan.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ karṇaparva procyate paramādbhutam sārathye viniyogaś ca madrarājasya dhīmataḥ ākhyātaṃ yatra paurāṇaṃ tripurasya nipātanam
english: From this point on the supremely marvellous Karṇa parvan is told; the appointment of the wise king of Madra as charioteer; and the ancient legend of the destruction of the triple city is narrated there.

sanskrit: prayāṇe paruṣaś cātra saṃvādaḥ karṇaśalyayoḥ haṃsakākīyam ākhyānam atraivākṣepasaṃhitam
english: And here during the march the harsh dialogue between Karṇa and Śalya; and the tale of the swan and the crow, full of reproach, is here as well.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ prati ca krodho yudhiṣṭhirakirīṭinoḥ dvairathe yatra pārthena hataḥ karṇo mahārathaḥ
english: And the mutual anger between Yudhiṣṭhira and Kirīṭin; and where the great warrior Karṇa was slain by Pārtha in single chariot combat.

sanskrit: aṣṭamaṃ parva nirdiṣṭam etad bhāratacintakaiḥ ekonasaptatiḥ proktā adhyāyāḥ karṇaparvaṇi catvāry eva sahasrāṇi nava ślokaśatāni ca
english: This eighth parvan has been designated by the scholars of the Bhārata; sixty-nine chapters are declared in the Karṇa parvan, and four thousand verses, and nine hundred verses more.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ vicitrārthaṃ śalyaparva prakīrtitam hatapravīre sainye tu netā madreśvaro 'bhavat
english: From this point on the Śalya parvan of manifold import is celebrated; when the foremost warriors of the army were slain, the lord of Madra became its leader.

sanskrit: vṛttāni rathayuddhāni kīrtyante yatra bhāgaśaḥ vināśaḥ kurumukhyānāṃ śalyaparvaṇi kīrtyate
english: The episodes of chariot battles are celebrated there in parts; the destruction of the chief Kurus is celebrated in the Śalya parvan.

sanskrit: śalyasya nidhanaṃ cātra dharmarājān mahārathāt gadāyuddhaṃ tu tumulam atraiva parikīrtitam sarasvatyāś ca tīrthānāṃ puṇyatā parikīrtitā
english: And here the death of Śalya at the hands of Dharmarāja the great warrior; and the tumultuous mace battle is celebrated here as well; and the sanctity of the tīrthas of the Sarasvatī is also celebrated.

sanskrit: navamaṃ parva nirdiṣṭam etad adbhutam arthavat ekonaṣaṣṭir adhyāyās tatra saṃkhyāviśāradaiḥ
english: This ninth parvan, marvellous and full of meaning, is designated; fifty-nine chapters are counted there by those skilled in enumeration.

sanskrit: saṃkhyātā bahuvṛttāntāḥ ślokāgraṃ cātra śasyate trīṇi ślokasahasrāṇi dve śate viṃśatis tathā muninā saṃpraṇītāni kauravāṇāṃ yaśobhṛtām
english: Many accounts are enumerated and the verse total is here celebrated: three thousand verses, two hundred and twenty more, composed by the sage in honour of the glorious Kauravas.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi sauptikaṃ parva dāruṇam bhagnoruṃ yatra rājānaṃ duryodhanam amarṣaṇam
english: From this point I shall speak of the dreadful Sauptika parvan, where the wrathful King Duryodhana lay with his thigh broken.

sanskrit: vyapayāteṣu pārtheṣu trayas te 'bhyāyayū rathāḥ kṛtavarmā kṛpo drauṇiḥ sāyāhne rudhirokṣitāḥ
english: When the Pārthas had withdrawn, three chariots approached — Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, and Drauṇi — at evening, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: pratijajñe dṛḍhakrodho drauṇir yatra mahārathaḥ ahatvā sarvapāñcālān dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamān pāṇḍavāṃś ca sahāmātyān na vimokṣyāmi daṃśanam
english: Where Drauṇi the great warrior, with firm anger, vowed: 'Without killing all the Pāñcālas headed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and the Pāṇḍavas together with their counsellors, I will not remove my armour.'

sanskrit: prasuptān niśi viśvastān yatra te puruṣarṣabhāḥ pāñcālān saparīvārāñ jaghnur drauṇipurogamāḥ
english: Where those bulls among men, led by Drauṇi, slaughtered the Pāñcālas along with their retinue in the night as they slept unsuspecting.

sanskrit: yatrāmucyanta pārthās te pañca kṛṣṇabalāśrayāt sātyakiś ca maheṣvāsaḥ śeṣāś ca nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Where those five Pārthas were saved through the protection of Kṛṣṇa's might, and the great archer Sātyaki too, while the rest met their deaths.

sanskrit: draupadī putraśokārtā pitṛbhrātṛvadhārditā kṛtānaśanasaṃkalpā yatra bhartṝn upāviśat
english: Where Draupadī, tormented by grief for her sons and afflicted by the slaughter of her father and brothers, having resolved to fast unto death, sat before her husbands.

sanskrit: draupadīvacanād yatra bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ anvadhāvata saṃkruddho bhāradvājaṃ guroḥ sutam
english: Where Bhīma of terrible valour, at Draupadī's words, furiously pursued the son of Bharadvāja, the teacher's son.

sanskrit: bhīmasenabhayād yatra daivenābhipracoditaḥ apāṇḍavāyeti ruṣā drauṇir astram avāsṛjat
english: Where Drauṇi, driven by fate and in fear of Bhīmasena, released his weapon in rage with the intent 'Let there be no Pāṇḍava offspring.'

sanskrit: maivam ity abravīt kṛṣṇaḥ śamayaṃs tasya tad vacaḥ yatrāstram astreṇa ca tac chamayām āsa phālgunaḥ
english: 'Not so,' said Kṛṣṇa, restraining his words; and there Phālguna appeased that weapon with a counter-weapon.

sanskrit: drauṇidvaipāyanādīnāṃ śāpāś cānyonyakāritāḥ toyakarmaṇi sarveṣāṃ rājñām udakadānike
english: The mutual curses exchanged among Drauṇi, Dvaipāyana, and others; and the water-rite, the offering of water to all the kings.

sanskrit: gūḍhotpannasya cākhyānaṃ karṇasya pṛthayātmanaḥ sutasyaitad iha proktaṃ daśamaṃ parva sauptikam
english: And the tale of Karṇa, son of Pṛthā, born in secret — this is here called the tenth parvan, the Sauptika.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśāsminn adhyāyāḥ parvaṇy uktā mahātmanā ślokāgram atra kathitaṃ śatāny aṣṭau tathaiva ca
english: Eighteen chapters are declared in this parvan by the great soul; the verse count stated here is eight hundred.

sanskrit: ślokāś ca saptatiḥ proktā yathāvad abhisaṃkhyayā sauptikaiṣīkasaṃbandhe parvaṇy amitabuddhinā
english: And seventy verses are declared, duly counted, in the parvan comprising the Sauptika and the Aiṣīka together, by the one of boundless intellect.
